editorial:
Imagine you are dropped right into the gritty streets of 1970s New York City, where everyone is looking for a payday and nobody can be trusted. You get to follow a group of small-time crooks who managed to pull off a huge heist, stealing $300,000 from the Italian mob. The problem is, they left a trail of bodies behind, including a few cops. Now, you have the mob and the police both hunting them down at the same time. It feels like a high-stakes game of cat and mouse where the tension never really lets up. You can tell right away that these guys are in over their heads, and that makes the whole ride feel dangerous and unpredictable.

What really makes this one work is how the plot twists and turns. The acting feels real, and the pacing keeps you on your toes without feeling rushed. While some of the older filming styles might feel a bit dated, the raw energy is still there. If you love old-school crime flicks with a lot of betrayal, you need to see this. It is a great pick if you are browsing for something to rent on Apple TV or if you want to hunt down the 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a huge betrayal. Just when you think the thieves might get away with the cash, the greed kicks in. The group turns on each other, and the police finally close in. In the end, the money doesn't buy anyone any freedom. Most of the criminals end up dead or captured, proving that stealing from the mob is a death sentence. It is a cynical ending where nobody really wins.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old-school crime stories and heist movies.
